what: official DeepSeek TileKernels TileLang Engram gate fwd/bwd made usable for the nano d12/d20 dims via exact power-of-two zero-padding; default path selection re-measured
problem: official kernels assert hidden_size % 256 == 0; naive next-multiple-of-256 padding uses c=sqrt(P/D)=sqrt(4/3), and storing c*x in bf16 rounds by ~0.4%, so the padded gate and its gradients differ from the reference (earlier D=384: gkv rel 0.42, gwh rel 0.52).
fix: grow P by factors of 4 (c=2^k exactly): x'=2x, key'=2key, w'=0.5w are exact in bf16; D=384->P=1536 (c=2), D=640->P=2560 (c=2), D=512 stays native (c=1). Chain rule: grad_x=c*grad_x'-(c-1)*grad_out, grad_key=c*grad_key', grad_value=grad_value', grad_w=(1/c)*grad_w'.

d12_tuned_graph_step_ms.shape: b=16 x seq=1024, graph-only, 2 rounds (same session)
d12_tuned_graph_step_ms.conclusion: padded official kernels are exact but 4x width -> slower than the Inductor-fused gate on d12; default remains: TL only for native hidden%256==0 (d16), padded TL opt-in via NANOV41_ENGRAM_TL_FORCE=1.
